chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Jamming at the Union against the separate locals' rules
summary: Lee describes being brought before the board for jamming and holding daily noon jam sessions in the practice hall, dodging the walking delegate Elmer Fayne.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let me ask you something -- you said you were in trouble for jamming. Didn't the union have -- I know later, the union had a rule that if you pay a basic rhythm section or if you pay 3 musicians -- a leader and 2 others -- then you can get permission to have a jam session where everybody isn't paid. Was that in effect then?
No, that came much later ... but I'll
tell you how that came about. That was forced. We forced their hands, and I'm still talking about the separate unions now.

We forced their hands because they had me before the Board so much where you couldn't jam, but they had a practice hall above the union, you know, at 1710 -- and all the people were doing business downstairs, but you could rehearse upstairs.

Well, no one ever rehearsed upstairs until like, six o'clock in the evening, when the union closed at five o'clock. And so they gave me so much heat and static about jamming, so I got the guys together -- there was Blanton, there was Nat -- and this time, really, I remember one time we had Charlie Christian upstairs, right?

And so I started calling the guys, and we started jamming, you know, and Eddie Barefield and Don -- and we started jamming in the day time at the union, and we would start at noon; we would start at 12 o'clock every day. And it would just drive the people crazy downstairs, you know?
And the walking delegate that used to catch me all the time -- his name was Elmer Fayne -- I'm sure you know him.
Right. So he would catch me every time, and he used to call me the "Fice" -- you know, he meant the little dog, you know -- the little Fice dog? He would say "You're just

like a little Fice; you cause all the trouble, you're always around jamming" -- but he never could stop me, because I wouldn't stop; you know, I was just kind of a revolutionary or something about it, because I was gonna play music, you know? And I wasn't gonna allow them to stop me.
